definitions.explanation: Having no equal anywhere: the strongest or best of all. A four-character idiom with a heroic, old-fashioned ring, used of warriors and champions and, often humorously, in games and sports.

examples.japanese: {天下無双|てんかむそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{剣士|けんし}→剣士：11912_kenshi⟧。
examples.english: A swordsman without equal in the land.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天下無双|てんかむそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{力持|ちからも}ち⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{知|し}られていた→知る：00458_shiru⟧。
examples.english: He was known as the strongest man in the land.

examples.japanese: ⟦{物語|ものがたり}→物語：03634_monogatari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{主人公|しゅじんこう}→主人公：11404_shujinkou⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{天下無双|てんかむそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{武将|ぶしょう}→武将：13222_bushou⟧だ⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{家族|かぞく}→家族：00552_kazoku⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{優|やさ}しい→優しい：02640_yasashii⟧⟦{父親|ちちおや}→父親：03469_chichioya⟧だった。
examples.english: The hero of the story was a peerless general, but at home he was a gentle father.

notes:
Made of ⟦{天下|てんか}→天下：12188_tenka⟧ (the whole land, the world) + ⟦{無双|むそう}→無双：32138_musou⟧ (without a pair, unmatched). The shorter ⟦{無双|むそう}→無双：32138_musou⟧ carries the same meaning and is common in games and slang.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {天下無双|てんかむそう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧〜: the peerless ~ (warrior, strength)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {国士無双|こくしむそう}: the greatest person in the land; also a mahjong hand
- ⟦{無敵|むてき}→無敵：21725_muteki⟧: invincible
